find: Upholding Proclamation No.~9645, President Trump's third entry-restriction order, the Court held 5--4 that \S~1182(f) gives the President broad power to suspend entry and that, under deferential rational-basis review, the facially neutral proclamation survived an Establishment Clause challenge; it also repudiated \textit{Korematsu}
replace: Reversing a preliminary injunction against President Trump's Proclamation No.~9645, the Court held 5--4 that \S~1182(f) gives the President broad power to suspend entry. Assuming it could look beyond the proclamation's facial neutrality under rational-basis review, the Court held that the plaintiffs had not shown a likelihood of success on their Establishment Clause challenge. It also repudiated \textit{Korematsu}
reason: The Court reviewed a preliminary injunction. It assumed for purposes of the case that it could look beyond the face of the proclamation rather than generally prescribing that level of scrutiny.

find: and a neutral text plus an agency process ordinarily suffices
replace: and evidence that the administration disregarded its own review or disabled the waivers could undermine the claimed justification
reason: The rational-basis analysis considered the substance of the review and the availability of waivers. The Court did not establish that facial neutrality and the mere existence of an agency process ordinarily suffice.

find: ``Plaintiffs challenge the entry suspension based on their perception of its effectiveness and wisdom, but the Court cannot substitute its own assessment for the Executive's predictive judgments on such matters.''
replace: ``More fundamentally, plaintiffs and the dissent challenge the entry suspension based on their perception of its effectiveness and wisdom. They suggest that the policy is overbroad and does little to serve national security interests. But we cannot substitute our own assessment for the Executive's predictive judgments on such matters, all of which `are delicate, complex, and involve large elements of prophecy.' ''
reason: The quoted sentence is the Reporter's syllabus (585 U.S. at 671), not the Chief Justice's opinion. It is replaced with the corresponding passage of the opinion, copied exactly from pages 707--708. The internal quotation from Chicago & Southern Air Lines is shown with single quotes.
The replacement passage begins at the foot of page 707 ('More fundamentally...') and ends on page 708.
